about: Homer Backs Into the Bushes is a short clip of Homer Simpson standing in front of a thick green hedge, looking uncomfortable, then slowly shuffling backward until the leaves swallow him completely. He never turns around or says a word; he just quietly removes himself from the situation. It is the internet's favorite way to say “I was never here.” People use it after an awkward moment, when a conversation turns against them, or when they realize they should not have joined a thread at all. The slow, silent exit is the joke.
origin: The scene is from The Simpsons episode “Homer Loves Flanders,” which first aired in 1994 during season 5, and it has been one of the most reused reaction GIFs ever since.
usage:
The top box sets up the uncomfortable moment, typically starting with “when” (“when someone asks”), and the bottom box finishes the question or situation you want to escape (“who broke production”). Homer's retreat is the reaction, so the caption should never explain it.

It lands best when you are guilty, out of your depth, or caught in a conversation you would rather leave: who ate the cake, who has done the reading, who knows the answer, who was supposed to bring the snacks.
